groups.title: Routing Concepts
groups.question: You are building a SvelteKit blog with a shared navbar and a page for each post. Explain how routing and layouts work.

followUps.File-based routing and the src/routes di: How does a folder in src/routes become a page?
followUps.Layouts and nested layout inheritance: How do layouts wrap pages and nest?
followUps.Dynamic route parameters with bracket sy: How do you read the slug in /blog/[slug]?

evidence.text: The folder structure maps to URLs.
A +page.svelte file in a folder is the page for that route.
The route tree is visible directly in the file system.
+layout.svelte wraps the pages below it with shared UI.
Nested folders can add their own layouts inside the parent ones.
Layouts stay in place when navigating between their child pages.
A folder named [slug] creates a dynamic segment.
The value is available as params.slug in load functions.
One route file serves every post.

groups.title: Error and Navigation
groups.question: A missing post crashes your page, and a new teammate does not know where to put shared utilities. Explain error pages and the project structure.

followUps.Error pages with +error.svelte boundary: What does +error.svelte do and how is it scoped?
followUps.SvelteKit project folder structure overv: What are src/routes, src/lib, static and svelte.config.js for?

evidence.text: +error.svelte shows a fallback when a load function throws an error.
Error pages in nested folders only cover their part of the app.
It can show the status and message, such as a 404 for a missing post.
src/routes holds pages, layouts and endpoints.
src/lib holds shared code, imported with $lib.
static holds files served as-is, and svelte.config.js configures the framework.

groups.title: Navigation and Links
groups.question: You need links between posts and a redirect to the new post after a form submit. Explain how navigation works in SvelteKit.

followUps.Client-side navigation with anchor tags: How does a plain <a> tag become client-side navigation?

evidence.text: SvelteKit intercepts normal links within the app automatically.
It loads the new page without a full reload.
No special Link component is needed.
goto navigates from code, like after a form submission.
It can replace the history entry instead of adding one.
Links are preferred for normal navigation because they work without JavaScript.

groups.title: Route Groups and Advanced Routing
groups.question: Marketing pages and the app need different layouts without changing URLs, and docs pages can be any depth. Explain route groups and rest parameters.

followUps.Route groups to share layouts without UR: What does a folder in parentheses do?

evidence.text: A route group organises routes without adding to the URL.
Each group can have its own layout.
Marketing pages and the app can share URL levels but use different layouts.
[...rest] matches any number of path segments.
[[optional]] makes a segment optional.
Rest suits catch-all docs pages; optional suits things like a language prefix.
